tools.name: cancel_workflow
tools.description:
Cancel a running CircleCI workflow, given its UUID (a workflow id
from list_run_workflows or get_workflow). Cancellation is asynchronous: a
successful call means the request was accepted, not that the workflow has
stopped yet.

workflow.description: The workflow UUID to cancel, as returned by list_run_workflows or get_workflow (each workflow's id).

tools.name: download_usage_data
tools.description:
Export a CircleCI organization's usage data as downloadable CSV files.
This is a two-phase, asynchronous tool. Phase 1 — start: call with org (an org
slug like "gh/acme" or an org UUID),
start_date, and end_date (both YYYY-MM-DD, a window of at most 31 days) and no
export_id; it returns an export_id. Phase 2 — poll/download: call again with that
export_id and the same org; once the export is ready it returns pre-signed
download URLs (no auth needed), or asks you to try again in a minute while it is
still being prepared. Optionally include shared_org_ids on Phase 1 to cover
additional organizations.

org.description: The billing organization whose usage to export, as either an org slug ("gh/acme") or an org UUID. Required on both phases.

start_date.description: Start of the export window, as YYYY-MM-DD. Required to start an export (Phase 1).

end_date.description: End of the export window, as YYYY-MM-DD. Required to start an export (Phase 1). The window must not exceed 31 days.

shared_org_ids.description: Optional additional organization UUIDs whose usage to include in the export (Phase 1).

export_id.description: The export id returned by a prior start call. Supply it together with org to poll for status and download URLs (Phase 2).

tools.name: get_deploy_component
tools.description:
Fetch a single CircleCI deploy component by its UUID (a component id from
list_deploy_components), returning its name and owning project ID.

component.description: The deploy component UUID, as returned by list_deploy_components.

tools.name: get_deploy_environment
tools.description:
Fetch a single CircleCI deploy environment by its UUID (an environment id
from list_deploy_environments), returning its name and owning org ID.

environment.description: The deploy environment UUID, as returned by list_deploy_environments.

tools.name: get_job
tools.description:
Fetch a single CircleCI job by its UUID (a job id from list_workflow_jobs),
returning its phase, outcome, and per-step detail including each step's
exit code — the signal for which step failed.

job.description: The job UUID, as returned by list_workflow_jobs (each job's id).

tools.name: get_job_logs
tools.description:
Fetch the stdout/stderr of a CircleCI job's steps, given the job's
UUID (a job id from list_workflow_jobs). With no step given, the failed steps are read
automatically — the fast path from a failing job to the output that explains
it — or the last step if none failed; pass step (a step's num from get_job) to
read any other. Output is rendered to plain text (ANSI escapes stripped,
progress-bar redraws collapsed) unless raw=true. tail_lines keeps only the
final lines of each step, where errors surface (defaults to 500, capped at
5000), and execution picks among a parallel job's executions. This is the
costliest way to inspect a job: read get_job first to learn which step to
ask for, and for a failing test step prefer list_job_tests.

job.description: The job UUID, as returned by list_workflow_jobs (each job's id).

step.description: A specific step to read, identified by its num from get_job. When omitted, the job's failed steps are read automatically; if no step failed, the last step is read. Name a step to read any other.

execution.description: For a job that ran with parallelism, the zero-based execution index to read. Defaults to 0 (the first execution).

tail_lines.description: Return only the last N lines of each step's output — where errors usually surface. Defaults to 500, capped at 5000. Output is limited by total size regardless of this value, and the truncated flag reports when anything was dropped.

raw.description: Return the raw terminal capture verbatim, keeping ANSI escapes and progress-bar redraws. Defaults to false, which renders the plain text a human would have seen. Because output is trimmed to its final lines, raw text may begin part-way through an escape sequence and will not carry styling set earlier in the log.

tools.name: get_job_resource_usage
tools.description:
Report how much CPU and memory a CircleCI job actually used, given the job's
UUID (a job id from list_workflow_jobs or get_job) — the signal for whether it is on the
right resource class, and for whether a failure was the executor running out.
Usage is sampled at a fixed interval for the length of each parallel execution
and summarised per execution against the limits of the resource class the job
ran on: cpu.* are in cores, memory.* in bytes, and peak_percent_of_limit is the
figure to read — under ~50% on both means a smaller class would fit, while
memory near 100% is what an OOM kill looks like. Set samples to also return the
series over time, which is what separates a steady load from a brief spike and
shows a memory leak's climb; leave it unset for the summary alone. A job that
ran with parallelism reports every execution unless execution names a single
zero-based index. A job that never ran an executor — an approval job, or one
cancelled before it started — has no usage to report and returns an error,
which does not mean the job is missing.

job.description: The job UUID, as returned by list_workflow_jobs or get_job (each job's id).

execution.description: For a job that ran with parallelism, a single zero-based execution index to report on. When omitted, every execution is reported.

samples.description: Also return the CPU and memory series over time, reduced to at most this many points per execution. Each point is the maximum of the samples it covers — so a brief spike is never averaged away — and series_interval_ms says how much time one point spans. Defaults to 0: summary statistics only. Capped at 200 per series, and reduced further to share a fixed total across a job with many parallel executions.

tools.name: get_me
tools.description:
Get details of the authenticated CircleCI user. Use this when a request
is about the user's own profile, or when information is missing to build
other tool calls (for example the caller's id or login).

tools.name: get_orb
tools.description:
Fetch a registry orb's metadata and published version history — given the orb
as "namespace/name" (e.g. "circleci/go") or an orb UUID; any @version suffix is
ignored, since the metadata covers the whole orb. Returns the latest version,
30-day usage stats, categories, and the list of published (stable) versions: the signal
for whether a version pinned in a config is stale and what to bump it to. Use get_orb_source
to read a specific version's definition.

orb.description: The orb to look up, as "namespace/name" (e.g. "circleci/go") or an orb UUID. Any @version suffix is ignored — the metadata is for the whole orb.

tools.name: get_orb_source
tools.description:
Fetch the YAML source of an orb version referenced by a CircleCI config —
given the orb as "namespace/name" optionally pinned to a version
("circleci/go@1.2.3", "@volatile" for latest, or a dev label "@dev:my-branch");
with no @version the latest published version is read. The source is the definition
of the commands, jobs, executors, and parameters the config invokes — read it to learn
how to call an orb correctly. Works only for registry orbs (namespace/name), not inline
or URL orbs.

orb.description: The orb to read, as "namespace/name" optionally pinned to a version: a semver ("circleci/go@1.2.3"), "@volatile" for the latest published version, or a dev label ("circleci/go@dev:my-branch"). With no @version, the latest published version is read.

tools.name: get_run
tools.description:
Fetch a single CircleCI run by its UUID (a run id from list_runs),
returning its phase, outcome, VCS details, and any config errors. The next
step in the CI-access chain: a run's id feeds list_run_workflows.

run.description: The run UUID, as returned by list_runs (each run's id).

tools.name: get_skill
tools.description:
Fetch one skill's guide as markdown, given its name (a skill's name from
list_skills) — the playbook to follow for the kind of work the skill
covers. Pass reference to load one of the skill's bundled references
instead of the guide, named by the path list_skills reports
("references/failure-patterns.md"); the guide says which of its references
to read and when, so load it first. The content is guidance for you, not an
answer for the user: read it, then act on it with the other tools.

skill.description: The skill's name, as returned by list_skills (each skill's name).

reference.description: Load one of the skill's bundled references instead of the guide, named by its path as list_skills reports it (e.g. "references/failure-patterns.md"). Omit to load the guide, which says which of its references to read and when.

tools.name: get_workflow
tools.description:
Fetch a single CircleCI workflow by its UUID (a workflow id from
list_run_workflows), returning its name, phase, and outcome. A workflow's id
feeds list_workflow_jobs.

workflow.description: The workflow UUID, as returned by list_run_workflows (each workflow's id).

tools.name: list_deploy_component_versions
tools.description:
List versions of a CircleCI deploy component — given the component's UUID
(a component id from list_deploy_components or get_deploy_component). Optionally
filter by deploy environment with the environment parameter. Versions come
newest-first, capped by limit (defaults to 20) — a long release history will set
truncated, so narrow by environment or raise limit for the rest.

component.description: The deploy component UUID, as returned by list_deploy_components or get_deploy_component.

environment.description: Optional: filter versions to those deployed in this environment UUID.

limit.description: Maximum number of versions to return, newest first. Defaults to 20; an actively deployed component can have far more, so any beyond the limit are omitted and reported via the truncated flag.

tools.name: list_deploy_components
tools.description:
List CircleCI deploy components for a project — given its slug
("gh/org/repo") or UUID. Deploy components are the deployable units of a
project (services, applications, libraries). Each component's id feeds
get_deploy_component and list_deploy_component_versions. limit caps how many are
returned (defaults to 20); truncated reports that more exist.

project.description: The project to list deploy components for, as a project slug ("gh/org/repo") or project UUID.

limit.description: Maximum number of components to return. Defaults to 20; any beyond the limit are omitted and reported via the truncated flag.

tools.name: list_deploy_environments
tools.description:
List CircleCI deploy environments for an organization — given its slug
("gh/myorg") or UUID. Deploy environments represent named targets such as
production or staging where components are released. Each environment's id feeds
get_deploy_environment and can filter list_deploy_component_versions. limit caps
how many are returned (defaults to 20); truncated reports that more exist.

org.description: The organization to list deploy environments for, as an org slug ("gh/myorg") or org UUID.

limit.description: Maximum number of environments to return. Defaults to 20; any beyond the limit are omitted and reported via the truncated flag.

tools.name: list_deployments
tools.description:
List recent CircleCI deployments newest-first with component name, version,
type, status, and timestamps. Pass project (slug "gh/org/repo" or UUID) to
scope to one project, or org (slug "gh/myorg" or UUID) to see deployments
across all projects in an org. Exactly one of project or org is required.
Use this to answer "what was last deployed" or "when was version X deployed"
without first looking up component or environment IDs. limit caps how many
are returned (defaults to 20); truncated reports that more exist.

project.description: The project to list deployments for, as a project slug ("gh/org/repo") or project UUID. Provide either project or org, not both.

org.description: The organization to list deployments for, as an org slug ("gh/myorg") or org UUID. Returns deployments across all projects in the org. Provide either org or project, not both.

limit.description: Maximum number of deployments to return, newest first. Defaults to 20; any beyond the limit are omitted and reported via the truncated flag.

tools.name: list_job_artifacts
tools.description:
List the artifacts a CircleCI job produced — the files it persisted
beyond the run, such as test reports, coverage, build outputs, or logs —
given the job's UUID (a job id from list_workflow_jobs or get_job). Each artifact
carries its path within the job, a URL to download it, and the parallel
execution that produced it — the same execution index get_job_logs reads and
get_job_resource_usage measures.

job.description: The job UUID whose artifacts to list, as returned by list_workflow_jobs or get_job (each job's id).

tools.name: list_job_tests
tools.description:
List a CircleCI job's test results, given the job's UUID (a job id
from list_workflow_jobs or get_job). By default only failing tests are returned — the
ones that explain a failure; set all=true to include passing and skipped
tests. Narrow further with filter ("result=...", "name=...",
"classname=..."), which are ANDed together; a result= filter replaces the
failing-only default. A job's full test set can be very large, so the number
returned is capped by limit (defaults to 100); when more tests matched than
were returned, truncated is true — narrow the filter or raise limit for the rest.

job.description: The job UUID whose test results to list, as returned by list_workflow_jobs or get_job (each job's id).

all.description: Include tests of every result (passing, skipped, failing), not just failing ones. Defaults to false — only failing tests are returned, which is almost always what you want when investigating a failure.

filter.description: Extra exact-match filters, each "key=value" where key is one of result, name, or classname (e.g. "classname=com.example.FooTest"). Repeatable; the filters are ANDed. Giving a result filter overrides the failing-only default.

limit.description: Maximum number of tests to return. Defaults to 100 and capped at 5000; a job's full test set can be very large, so any matches beyond the limit are omitted and reported via the truncated flag. A total size budget also applies, so a request for many tests with long failure messages may return fewer than the limit.

tools.name: list_run_workflows
tools.description:
List the workflows belonging to a CircleCI run, given the run's UUID
(a run id from list_runs or get_run). The next step in the CI-access chain:
each workflow's id feeds get_workflow and list_workflow_jobs.

run.description: The run UUID whose workflows to list, as returned by list_runs or get_run (each run's id).

tools.name: list_runs
tools.description:
List CircleCI runs for a project — given its slug ("gh/org/repo")
or UUID — or the authenticated user's own runs across all projects (mine=true).
Optionally filter by pipeline status, and — for a project, but not for
mine=true, which has no branch filter — by git branch. limit caps how many are
returned (defaults to 10). This is the entry point of the CI-access tool chain;
each run's id feeds get_run and the workflow/job tools.

project.description: Project locator: either a slug ("gh/org/repo") or a project UUID. Required unless mine is true.

mine.description: List runs the authenticated user triggered across all projects, instead of a single project. When true, project and branch are ignored.

branch.description: Only list runs on this git branch. Ignored when mine is true.

status.description: Only list runs with this pipeline status, e.g. "success", "failed", "running", "on_hold".

limit.description: Maximum number of runs to return. Defaults to 10.

tools.name: list_skills
tools.description:
List the skills this server ships: written playbooks for the jobs that
take several of its tools, saying which tool answers a given question, in
what order, and what to skip. Each entry carries the skill's name for
get_skill, a description of what it covers, the references it bundles, and
the resource URI the same guide is readable at. Takes no arguments and
returns the whole catalog. Call this at the start of a piece of work rather
than after one has gone wrong.

tools.name: list_workflow_jobs
tools.description:
List the jobs belonging to a CircleCI workflow, given the workflow's
UUID (a workflow id from list_run_workflows or get_workflow). The next step in
the CI-access chain: each job's id feeds get_job.

workflow.description: The workflow UUID whose jobs to list, as returned by list_run_workflows or get_workflow (each workflow's id).

tools.name: rerun_workflow
tools.description:
Rerun a CircleCI workflow, given its UUID (a workflow id from
list_run_workflows or get_workflow). By default every job reruns from the
start; set from_failed=true to rerun only the failed jobs and everything
downstream of them, reusing the successful ones. A rerun creates a new
workflow, whose id is returned to follow the new run.

workflow.description: The workflow UUID to rerun, as returned by list_run_workflows or get_workflow (each workflow's id).

from_failed.description: Rerun only the failed jobs (and everything downstream of them), reusing the successful jobs. Defaults to false, which reruns every job from the start.

tools.name: rollback_deploy_component
tools.description:
DANGEROUS — redeploys production software. Roll a deployed CircleCI component
back to an earlier version. Requires the project (slug "gh/org/repo" or UUID),
the component UUID (from list_deploy_components), the environment UUID it is
deployed to (from list_deploy_environments), the version currently deployed, and
the target version to roll back to (from list_deploy_component_versions or
list_deployments). Confirm the plan with the user before calling: name the
component, the environment, and both versions, and pass their stated reason as
reason — it is recorded in the audit log. current_version is a safety check, not
a formality: read it from the deploy tools rather than assuming, because the
rollback is refused when it is not the version actually deployed. Optionally
scope the component with namespace, and steer the rollback pipeline with
checkout_ref, config_ref, and parameters. Depending on the project's deploy
settings the rollback is carried out by a pipeline run or by a release-agent
command — rollback_type says which and id is that run or command — so a
successful call means the rollback started, not that the target version is live;
follow the returned id to confirm.

project.description: The project the component belongs to, as a project slug ("gh/org/repo") or project UUID.

component.description: The deploy component UUID to roll back, as returned by list_deploy_components.

environment.description: The deploy environment UUID the component is deployed to, as returned by list_deploy_environments.

current_version.description: The version currently deployed. The rollback is refused unless this really is the deployed version, so read it from list_deployments or list_deploy_component_versions rather than guessing.

target_version.description: The earlier version to roll back to, as returned by list_deploy_component_versions.

namespace.description: Optional: the namespace scoping the component within the environment. Defaults to "default".

reason.description: Optional: why the rollback was requested. Recorded in the audit log — supply the user's stated reason.

parameters.description: Optional: extra parameters passed to the rollback pipeline, as a map of name to value. Ignored when the project has no rollback pipeline configured.

checkout_ref.description: Optional: the git ref the rollback pipeline checks out. Defaults to the project's default branch; ignored when the project has no rollback pipeline configured.

config_ref.description: Optional: the git ref the rollback pipeline's config is read from. Defaults to the project's default branch; ignored when the project has no rollback pipeline configured.

tools.name: send_feedback
tools.description:
Send feedback about this server to CircleCI: an error that looks like a
CircleCI fault, a capability you needed and could not find, or a tool whose
output or description misled you. message is the report itself, up to 2000
characters — say what you were trying to do, which tools you called and what
happened; leave out secrets. tool optionally names the tool the report is
about (e.g. "get_job_logs"), up to 200 characters. A report records the
authenticated CircleCI user and the client's name, and returns the report's
id. Send one report per distinct problem.

message.description: The report itself, up to 2000 characters: what you were trying to do, which tools you called and what happened. Leave out secrets.

tool.description: The tool the report is about (e.g. "get_job_logs"), up to 200 characters. Omit it for a report that is not about one tool.

tools.name: validate_config
tools.description:
Validate a CircleCI pipeline config by compiling it — the equivalent of the
`circleci config validate` CLI command. Pass the raw config YAML (the contents of
.circleci/config.yml) as config; the server expands orbs, resolves parameter expressions,
and expands matrix jobs, returning valid=true on success or valid=false with the
compilation errors on failure. Supply org (a slug like "gh/acme" or a
UUID) whenever the config references anything org-scoped: private registry orbs, or URL
orbs — any orb whose value is a URL rather than "namespace/name@version", which are gated
by the org's URL orb allow-list. Without org, only public registry orbs resolve, so those
references fail with errors like "not permitted by the organization's URL orb allow-list"
or "orb not found" — these are false negatives from missing org context, NOT real config
problems, so before reporting a config invalid, check whether it declares private or URL
orbs and if so retry with org. set preview_next=true to preview upcoming,
potentially breaking config changes; pass pipeline_parameters to resolve
<< pipeline.parameters.* >> expressions, and pipeline_values for the wider
<< pipeline.* >> template context (e.g. "pipeline.git.branch") when a config
depends on it.

config.description: The raw CircleCI pipeline config YAML to validate (the contents of .circleci/config.yml). Required.

org.description: Organization slug ("gh/acme") or UUID. Optional; supply it to resolve the org's private orbs during compilation. Without it, only public orbs resolve.

preview_next.description: Enable "config next" to preview upcoming, potentially breaking config changes. Defaults to false.

pipeline_parameters.description: Values injected at << pipeline.parameters.* >> expressions, as a map of parameter name to value. Optional.

pipeline_values.description: Advanced: the << pipeline.* >> template context (e.g. "pipeline.git.branch"), as a flat map of CircleCI template identifier to value. Optional; usually unnecessary.
